title: Check yourself: composition in concurrent code

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A booking service extends `ConcurrentHashMap<String, String>` with `synchronized boolean reserve(String seat, String customer) { if (containsKey(seat)) return false; put(seat, customer); return true; }`. A partner integration books seats on the same object through the map's own `putIfAbsent(seat, customer)`. Both are called for seat 14C at the same moment. What can happen?

options.text: The seat is booked once, since the `synchronized` on `reserve` also covers the map's inherited methods
options.says: the subclass's monitor excludes only code that locks this; the inherited methods keep the base's own locking

options.text: The seat can be booked twice, since `putIfAbsent` never waits for the monitor `reserve` holds
options.says: a synchronized subclass method locks this, and ConcurrentHashMap's methods never lock the map object, so putIfAbsent can run between containsKey and put

options.text: The seat can be booked twice, since `reserve` and `putIfAbsent` each lock their own bin of the map
options.says: reserve is a synchronized method, so it locks the subclass object itself, not a bin; two calls of reserve can't overlap

options.text: The seat is booked once, since `containsKey` and `put` are each atomic in a `ConcurrentHashMap`
options.says: each call is atomic, and another thread's putIfAbsent can still run between the two

origin.section: A Subclass's synchronized Method Excludes Only Code That Locks this

questions.stem: A shop keeps carts in one `Collections.synchronizedMap(new HashMap<>())`. Each incoming request builds a new `CartService` over that map, whose `synchronized Cart cartFor(String user)` calls `get` and, if it returned null, `put`s a new cart. A user's browser sends two requests at once for a user with no cart yet. What follows?

options.text: The user can end up with two carts, since the wrapper runs `get` and `put` without its lock
options.says: each wrapper call takes the wrapper's lock whoever calls it; the gap is between the two calls

options.text: The user can end up with two carts, since each request's `CartService` is a different lock
options.says: the synchronized method locks the service, one per request, so nothing excludes the two get-then-put sequences on the shared map

options.text: The user gets one cart, since each request's `CartService` runs `cartFor` with its lock held
options.says: each CartService holds its own lock, and there is one per request, so the two calls don't exclude each other

options.text: The user gets one cart, since the wrapper keeps its lock across the whole of `cartFor`
options.says: the wrapper locks each call and releases the lock between get and put

origin.section: A Helper Outside the Class Must Take the Lock the Class Takes

questions.stem: A `RecipientSet` keeps a `List<String>` field and guards its `addNew` (add the address unless it is there) and `snapshot()` methods with a private lock object. Its constructor stores the list the caller passes in, `new RecipientSet(recipients)`, and the caller keeps `recipients` and runs `if (!recipients.contains(a)) recipients.add(a)` from a nightly job. Can an address end up stored twice?

options.text: No, since the job's check and add fall before or after each locked `addNew`, never inside it
options.says: nothing makes the job's unlocked calls wait for RecipientSet's lock, so they can land between addNew's check and its add

options.text: No, if `recipients` is a synchronized list, since the job's `add` then waits for `RecipientSet`'s lock
options.says: the wrapper's add locks the wrapper, not RecipientSet's private lock object

options.text: Yes, since `snapshot()` can copy the list while `addNew` is halfway through
options.says: snapshot and addNew hold the same private lock, so a copy never sees addNew halfway, and copying stores nothing

options.text: Yes, since the job's check and add take no lock that `RecipientSet` holds
options.says: the class is safe only while no reference to its state escapes; the caller's own reference is a path around the lock

origin.section: A Class That Owns the State and the Lock Doesn't Depend on What It Wraps

questions.stem: A gateway finds a backend session with `Session fresh = Session.open(id); Session old = sessions.putIfAbsent(id, fresh); return old != null ? old : fresh;` on a `ConcurrentHashMap`, where `Session.open` opens a TCP connection. Most requests are for ids that already have a session. What does the backend see?

options.text: A new connection for every request, since `putIfAbsent` stores each newly opened session over the old one
options.says: putIfAbsent keeps the existing mapping and returns it; the extra session is thrown away, not stored

options.text: One connection per id, since `Session.open` runs only once `putIfAbsent` finds the key absent
options.says: the argument is evaluated before the call, so Session.open runs on every call; computeIfAbsent, by contrast, builds the value only when the key is absent

options.text: One connection per id, since `putIfAbsent` is atomic, so each session is opened once
options.says: atomicity covers the check and the put; it can't undo the construction that ran before the call

options.text: A new connection for every request, since `Session.open` runs before `putIfAbsent` looks at the key
options.says: the value is an argument, so it is built on every call; putIfAbsent only decides whether to keep it

origin.section: putIfAbsent Builds the Value Before It Knows It Is Needed

concepts: The composed class's guarantee holds only while no reference to its state escapes: a list stored from the caller, or returned by a getter, is a path around the lock.

A helper's synchronized method locks the helper, so helpers created per request or per tenant over one shared collection exclude nothing; the helper must take the lock the collection itself takes, which works only where the collection documents it, as Collections.synchronizedList does.

A synchronized method added by a subclass locks this, so it excludes only code that locks this; over a base that locks a private object, such as CopyOnWriteArrayList or ConcurrentHashMap, the base's own methods run straight through it.
